note: Chelban et al. (2020) confirmed that neonatal-onset NKX6-2 disease shows a significantly higher frequency of global psychomotor developmental delay compared to later childhood-onset cases, which primarily present with a motor spastic ataxia phenotype.

evidence.text: The neonatal-onset group has a statistically significant higher frequency of global psychomotor developmental delay compared with the other onset groups, reflecting a phenotypic spectrum ranging from neonatal onset with global delay to childhood onset with a mainly motor phenotype.

source.title: Genetic and phenotypic characterization of NKX6‐2‐related spastic ataxia and hypomyelination
source.quote: The neonatal-onset group has a statistically significant higher frequency of global psychomotor developmental delay (red) compared with the other two groups (onset from 2 months … Our data reveal a phenotype spectrum with neonatal onset, global psychomotor delay and worse prognosis at the severe end and a childhood onset with mainly motor phenotype at the milder end.

evidence.text: At the milder end of the NKX6-2 disease spectrum, individuals achieve normal early motor milestones in the first year of life before developing slowly progressive spastic ataxia.

source.title: NKX6-2-related disorder
source.quote: At the milder end of the spectrum is normal achievement of early motor milestones in the first year of life followed by slowly progressive complex spastic ataxia with pyramidal findings
